summary.text: James Rutledge, a Republican Harford County attorney of about four decades, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Attorney General of Maryland to Anthony Brown.
He served as a Bel Air town commissioner from November 2023 to October 2025.

paragraphs.text: Rutledge graduated with honors from the University of Maryland School of Law and is licensed to practice in Maryland and Georgia, with more than 30 years of practice.
In 2022 he served on the Judicial Nominating Commission for District and Circuit Court judges in Harford County.
He was elected a Bel Air town commissioner in November 2023 and served until October 2025.
During the campaign, he emphasized crime, support for law enforcement and keeping the office from suing the federal government over policy disagreements.
He received 31.6% of the vote to Anthony Brown's 68.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: Rutledge faces steep climb to unseat Brown in low-key attorney general's race
